statement: The Rothera coastal time series yielded 7,957 mid- to high-quality vOTUs, about 75% of which lacked species-level representation in the comparison ocean-virus catalogues.
Viral genomes beneath the Ross Ice Shelf were computationally linked to ammonia-oxidizing Nitrosopumilus hosts, alongside transcriptional evidence that viruses were active.
Pristine Antarctic soil metagenomes contained diverse Class 1 CRISPR–Cas systems and divergent Class 2 type-V architectures, including unusual Cas12-like effectors.
A comparative survey of polar and temperate lakes recovered 3,304 giant-virus MAGs spanning all recognized Nucleocytoviricota orders and found strong lake-level endemism.
Caudoviricetes accounted for more than 90% of viral relative abundance in contaminated King George Island soils, compared with less than 62% in uncontaminated soils.
At the HAUSGARTEN Arctic time-series site, viral community composition recurred annually and tracked prokaryotic community composition across four years.
Arctic sea-surface-microlayer vOTUs encoded candidate ice-binding and glycerol-related auxiliary genes that could contribute to cryoprotection.
Stable-isotope probing identified 243 active viral populations under anoxic sub-freezing peat conditions, with one-third linked to active bacterial populations.
Ancient Siberian permafrost metagenomes contained prominent Pithoviridae-like sequences, including a complete 1.6-Mb circular genome from an approximately 42,000-year-old sample.
Global comparative analyses separated polar from non-polar giant-virus communities and identified temperature as a major correlate of virus–host network structure.
Culture-based screening isolated five marseilleviruses and five megaviruses from diverse natural and human-influenced sites above the Arctic Circle.
Single-cell genomics recovered extensive and largely novel Patescibacteria diversity among 1,374 SAGs from Mercer Subglacial Lake.
Early glacier-foreland colonizers encoded flexible energy strategies that included potential oxidation of atmospheric trace gases and sulfur compounds.
Complete-ammonia-oxidizing Nitrospira genomes were prominent in the sampled coastal Antarctic soils and encoded traits consistent with cold stress protection and high substrate affinity.
The data resource combines long-read, Hi-C, and single-cell genomic datasets from two rarely sampled Antarctic geothermal systems.
Antarctic sponges contained many host-exclusive prokaryotic ASVs: 76% of bacterial and archaeal ASVs were sponge-exclusive in the reported dataset.
A multi-year autonomous time series resolved five recurring temporal microbiome modules representing distinct seasonal ecological states.
The MOSAiC catalogue contains 2,407 prokaryotic MAGs and 56 eukaryotic MAGs from 73 Central Arctic samples spanning a full seasonal cycle and multiple habitats.
Atlantic inflow and reduced ice favored seasonally fluctuating populations, while densely ice-covered waters retained a comparatively stable resident microbiome.
The dominant Tariuqbacteria genome from Lake A's anoxic relict seawater layer supports a strictly anaerobic lifestyle with sulfur or sulfate reduction and versatile carbon metabolism.
The Arctic Ocean genome catalogue represents 526 species, of which 441 had not previously been reported and 299 appeared exclusively polar in the comparison data.
Across 218 circumpolar metagenomes, water-mass identity was a dominant organizer of prokaryotic gene composition, with many genes showing bipolar yet Southern-Ocean-enriched distributions.
The resource releases 319 bacterial MAGs from soils on Deception and Livingston islands, expanding reference coverage for maritime Antarctic soil lineages.
Maxwell Bay community assembly shifted toward 84.68% deterministic homogeneous selection in February, consistent with stronger late-summer environmental filtering.
Seasonal molecular observations identified symbiotic UCYN-A among prominent diazotrophs where measured nitrogen fixation supported coastal productivity near West Greenland.
A 25-year synthesis estimated declining summer diatom chlorophyll and increasing haptophyte and cryptophyte chlorophyll, followed by partial reversal after the 2016 sea-ice regime change.

After an approximately 7% step decrease in September sea-ice extent, mean spring diatom contribution rose by as much as about 10% in sea-ice-influenced regions but declined on parts of the summer shelf.
A four-year Fram Strait series supports a winter reset in which prevailing winter conditions strongly constrained the microeukaryotes present in the following spring bloom.
Antarctic benthic responses to warming and cryosphere change are regionally heterogeneous, with local disturbance, freshening, sediment, and species traits determining biomass gains or losses.
High-Arctic fjords supported more trophically diverse picoeukaryotes, whereas warmer fjords showed a larger prokaryotic contribution to the 0.2–3-µm community.
Darkening by visible algal blooms contributed up to 2.4% of total modeled surface melt under observed conditions on the Antarctic ice cap.
Antarctic plastic debris carried eukaryotic communities rich in diatom-lineage Gyrista, fungi, and arthropods, alongside Pseudomonadota- and Bacteroidota-dominated prokaryotic records.

Diatoms and euphausiid fecal pellets dominated collected biogenic particles, and autumn particulate-organic-carbon export was comparable to the summer pulse at this coastal West Antarctic Peninsula site.

Across a 13.3-kyr sedimentary ancient-DNA record, major climatic and water-mass transitions reorganized eukaryotic assemblages mainly through species replacement while many functional roles persisted.
Arctic shelves, basins, ridges, and gateways steer current pathways and modify mixing and ventilation, coupling geological architecture to modern hydrography.
Antarctic Bottom Water ventilates the abyss and redistributes heat, carbon, oxygen, and nutrients after dense shelf waters descend the continental slope.
Wind-driven opening, rapid sea-ice production, and brine rejection make Antarctic coastal polynyas key formation sites for dense shelf water.
Southern Ocean ecosystems export a globally important quantity of biologically produced carbon through sinking particles and dissolved organic matter.
The regional model projects an approximately 40% decline in Arctic biological-carbon-pump efficiency by 2100 under the analyzed climate scenario.
The reconstruction attributes at least half of Arctic benthic denitrification to the broad, shallow Siberian shelf system and shows a rapid increase after the 2009 sea-ice regime transition.
More than 600 Antarctic subglacial lakes have been identified, and repeated filling and drainage show that some participate in dynamic, material-transporting hydrological networks.
Airborne magnetic patterns reveal multiple subglacial crustal domains and structural boundaries around Dome Fuji that record assembly and reworking across supercontinent cycles.
The Amerasia Basin comprises distinct crustal provinces whose evolution involves Canada Basin opening, terrane motion, and Alpha–Mendeleev magmatism rather than one simple spreading episode.
Exposed East Antarctic rocks preserve a discontinuous Archean-to-Cambrian record of crustal formation, metamorphism, and Gondwanan assembly.
The modeled Arctic continental slope carries a disproportionate share of advective dissolved-inorganic-nitrogen transport despite occupying only a small fraction of Arctic Ocean area.
Model experiments estimate that rivers and coastal erosion sustain approximately 28–51% of contemporary Arctic Ocean net primary production through nutrient delivery and shelf recycling.
At sampled offshore Southern Ocean stations, combined iron and manganese addition stimulated stronger phytoplankton growth and major-nutrient drawdown than iron alone.
Iceberg A-68A released an estimated 152 ± 61 Gt of freshwater within 300 km of South Georgia between November 2020 and March 2021.
Stable-isotope-constrained inversion attributed approximately 80% of river sulfate in the studied Koyukuk watershed to sulfide oxidation.
The ultraslow-spreading Gakkel Ridge hosts hydrothermal activity amid strong along-axis variation in magmatism, tectonic extension, and crustal construction.

In EC-Earth3 under SSP5-8.5, prescribed Greenland runoff and calving added about 0.9 sverdrups per century of AMOC weakening through 2100 and approximately 4 sverdrups of weakening by 2300 relative to the no-added-meltwater ensemble.
Tropical mean-state biases, especially in the ITCZ and surface winds, weaken the simulated tropical response to Southern Ocean cooling across the analyzed climate-model hierarchy.
Idealized Antarctic meltwater cooling produces a remote tropical surface response that is amplified when the background winds permit a stronger wind-evaporation-sea-surface-temperature feedback.
Curated lineage-dominant CAN SINE insertions in sampled polar and brown bears were concentrated in untranslated, upstream, and other candidate regulatory regions rather than protein-coding sequence.

The analyzed polar-bear genomes contain lineage-dominant transposable-element-associated structural variants, including fixed derived insertions near genes proposed as candidates for polar-bear and brown-bear phenotypic divergence.
Ice-mass and glacial-isostatic-adjustment models project approximately 0.41 to 0.93 metres of relative sea-level fall near Aasiaat by 2100 across the analyzed RCP2.6 and RCP8.5 cases.

Combining projected relative sea-level fall with newly mapped shallow thresholds indicates that the Nivaaq and Ikerasannguaq channels may shoal or close, reducing navigation access and potentially coastal water and nutrient exchange.
Benthic microbial mats from Arctic, Antarctic, and sub-Antarctic lakes share a functional core that includes genes for phosphorus acquisition and cycling alongside broad stress-response functions.

The statistical lagged influence of the spring Southern Annular Mode on Antarctic summer sea ice strengthened after approximately 1998 through a stronger PSA-like circulation and Amundsen Sea Low pathway.

Svalbard fjord surface sediments contain microbial genes and expressed enzymes capable of degrading complex land-derived carbohydrates, showing that a biologically available fraction persists after burial.
Bayelva active-layer microbial genomes and transcripts encode broad carbohydrate-degradation pathways that provide a terrestrial functional baseline for comparison with Svalbard fjord sediments.
H2-18O quantitative stable-isotope probing resolved distinct early and late microbial growers after active-layer soil thaw, with only 22% of labeled sequence variants growing at both 21 and 98 days.

Growth after thaw included Myxococcota, Patescibacteria, and Bdellovibrionota affiliated with predatory or epibiotic lifestyles, indicating that cell-cell interactions contribute to post-thaw turnover.
Highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b genotype B3.2 was confirmed in all three sampled Tristan skua carcasses from Gough Island, and two samples yielded viral whole-genome sequences.
Phylogenetic source-sink reconstruction and skua tracking support a plausible South Georgia-to-Gough H5N1 dispersal pathway, but do not directly observe movement by an infected bird.

The Jonah's icefish reference resource contains a 1.27-gigabase assembly with 96.8% of sequence anchored to 24 chromosomes, a scaffold N50 of 51.82 megabases, and 31,777 predicted protein-coding genes.
MpoV-44T.A and MpoV-44T.B are independently replicating lytic dsDNA viruses of Micromonas polaris, but they differ substantially in genome sequence, host range, infectivity, and lysis timing.

When equal particle numbers of both viruses were added to the shared host, MpoV-44T.B genome production reached only 18 plus or minus 8% of its single-infection production, whereas MpoV-44T.A production was not significantly reduced.

MpoV-44T.B-like reads were consistently more abundant than MpoV-44T.A-like reads in the analyzed Tara Arctic metagenomes, reversing the competitive ordering seen in the nutrient-replete dual-infection experiment.

All four Antarctic fur-seal fecal metagenomes contained chitin-degradation genes, and MAGs assigned complementary hydrolytic steps to different bacterial taxa, consistent with cross-feeding on a krill-rich diet.

The four fecal metagenomes contained 16 annotated antimicrobial-resistance gene types, including bacitracin, polymyxin, and multidrug categories, but these sequences do not establish phenotypic resistance or anthropogenic selection.
Bulk metagenomes from nine Arctic, Baltic, and Antarctic sea-ice samples yielded 550 vOTUs, with 528 of 537 classified vOTUs assigned to Caudoviricetes.
Hosts were computationally assigned to 187 sea-ice vOTUs, with Gammaproteobacteria and Bacteroidia the most frequent predicted host classes.
Austral-winter Southern Ocean sea ice contained 24–115 nanomolar total DMSP, 2–38 times the concentrations measured in contemporaneous seawater samples.

DSYB- and DSYE-bearing eukaryotic algae were predicted to dominate DMSP biosynthetic potential, while bacterial producers and abundant dmdA, dddD, and dddK genes expanded the inferred producer–consumer network.
The estimated turbulent silicic-acid flux across the ice–ocean interface was similar in magnitude to the silicon demand inferred for the observed ice-algal bloom.
A Nitzschia-frigida-rich bottom-ice bloom fixed 146 ± 4.8 milligrams carbon per square metre per day and accumulated 42.4 ± 1.6 milligrams chlorophyll a per square metre.
Glacial bacterial lineages dominated foreland MAGs but were rare in fjord MAGs, indicating strong filtering between the glacier–foreland system and coastal seawater.
Genome-resolved pathway profiles separated carbon-fixation potential concentrated in glacial MAGs, a foreland denitrification hotspot, and sulfur-oxidation potential dominant in the fjord.

The Amundsen sea-ice zone showed selective total-iron enrichment relative to offshore waters without comparable enrichment of the other measured metals, a pattern consistent with sea-ice melt supplying iron.

Five-day iron additions produced little chlorophyll response in the polynya, a larger offshore response, and a highly variable sea-ice-zone response, showing that iron sensitivity differs across Amundsen hydrographic regimes.
A two-year Ross Sea eDNA survey detected 92 eukaryotic species in both 2024 and 2025, including Antarctic diatoms and dinoflagellates.
Thermal stratification and water-mass properties were the leading measured correlates of vertical and horizontal Ross Sea eukaryotic community separation.
Dispersed-oil and dispersant-only ice showed early enrichment of Gammaproteobacteria, including Oleispira, Bermanella, and Pseudoalteromonas, relative to clean experimental ice.
Oil- and dispersant-exposed experimental sea ice accumulated hydrocarbon-degradation gene potential, but heavy hydrocarbons showed less than 10% depletion after 89 days.
MOSAiC pressure ridges contained unique communities and summer algal biomass up to eight-fold higher than level ice or surface water.
For a 40-square-kilometre MOSAiC area in July, ridges occupying 22% of sea-ice area were estimated to contain 80 ± 20% of area-integrated ice-associated chlorophyll a.
Highly porous July rotten ice near Utqiaġvik contained prokaryotic communities distinct from earlier-season ice and vertically homogeneous within each floe.
Despite drainage and vertical homogenization of dissolved properties, rotten ice retained particulate carbon, nitrogen, and extracellular polymeric material toward its upper horizons.

During a 49-hour Fram Strait melt experiment, about one-tenth of bacterial and microeukaryotic taxa in original sea ice were directly traceable in meltwater, with larger cells and aggregates contributing strongly.
Ten of 128 molecular formulae unique to original sea ice were subsequently detected in meltwater, providing a chemical fingerprint of ice-to-water connectivity.
ANME lineages occupied different sediment niches: ANME-2a/b predominated in upper and middle sulfate–methane transition layers, whereas ANME-1b was more prominent in deeper sulfate-depleted layers.
Microbial assemblages differed among hydrate-bearing, transition, and carbonate zones; ANME-1b occurred prominently in hydrate-bearing intervals.
Particle-attached and free-living prokaryotic fractions differed in abundance and diversity; free-living communities were more associated with temperature and inorganic nutrients.
DNA- and RNA-derived assemblages differed, with RNA libraries showing stronger representation of methane-cycling archaea and sulfate reducers in particular seep habitats.
The 110 recovered sulfur-cycling genomes supported distinct niches above and below SMTZ, linking inferred sulfur metabolism with carbon fixation and nitrogen fixation.
Bottom-water bacterial composition differed among seep-intensity regimes; the high-intensity site had the lowest alpha diversity and methane was associated with community variation.
The study supplied 768 MAGs from Site F samples, including 597 bacterial and 171 archaeal genomes, expanding genomic references across seep compartments.
Communities grouped by methane-supply regime across sites, with ANME-1 more prominent under high supply and ANME-2 under low supply.
Abundant populations carried and expressed macromolecule-fermentation pathways, while classical sulfate reducers, methanogens, and methanotrophs were comparatively rare.
Population genomes showed generally low homologous recombination and strong purifying selection, with sediment-depth-dependent diversification of key metabolic genes.
Geochemical, omics, and model evidence supported an additional methane sink linked to iron and manganese reduction in methanic sediments.
The study provided incubation evidence for nitrate/nitrite-dependent methane oxidation in addition to sulfate-associated pathways in SCS seep sediments.
Culture and transcript evidence linked Campylobacterota to hydrogen utilization, sulfur transformations, and nitrate consumption at the seep interface.
The study recovered 338 vOTUs and identified candidate viral persistence strategies alongside low within-population nucleotide diversity.
Fungal sequences occupied connected network positions and fungal genes were transcribed in seep sediments, supporting inclusion of fungi in seep-microbiome studies.
Seep and reference samples differed in elemental distribution and bacterial network structure; water and sediment assemblages were more similar at seepage stations.
Prokaryotic diversity and modeled assembly processes changed with depth and hydrochemistry, with Cyanobacteria prominent near the illuminated surface and Proteobacteria deeper.
Interface microbiomes differed between Lingshui and Site F, with distinct inferred methane-, nitrogen-, and sulfur-associated functional profiles.
Upper active-seep sediments contained more Hg and methylmercury than reference sediments, alongside genes associated with mercury transformations.
Nitrogen fixation occurred in Haima water and increased following sulfur-containing organic-matter enrichment; Dechloromonas genomes carried nitrogen-fixation and sulfur-oxidation genes.
Prokaryotes generally had lower diversity in seep sediments than reference sediments, whereas microeukaryotes showed the opposite pattern; DNA/RNA differences were larger for microeukaryotes.
The 377 MAGs supported vertical metabolic differentiation, including methanotrophic populations from bottom-interface water into deeper mesopelagic layers.
LucaPCycle expanded phosphorus-cycling protein detection, revealing archaeal and viral genetic potential and validating selected previously unannotated phosphatases.
Reductive-dehalogenase-like genes occurred across diverse archaeal and bacterial groups, with complementary chemical and experimental evidence supporting organohalide-transforming potential.
Multiple signaling systems were detected across seep taxa, and representative LuxI–LuxR pairs showed activity in heterologous tests.
Sponge microbiomes had distinct composition, lower diversity, and enrichment of specialized sulfur- and methane-associated bacterial groups compared with environmental microbiomes.
The comparative catalog revealed extensive defense and anti-defense diversity, and selected candidate microbial systems protected against viral infection in laboratory assays.
Near-seep and deeper-water communities showed greater representation of methane- and sulfur-associated populations and genes, indicating spatially structured metabolic potential.
Microbial diversity and co-occurrence varied by compartment and habitat; modeled environmental selection differed between prokaryotes and microeukaryotes in water versus sediment.
Nitrate/nitrite-coupled methane oxidation had a larger potential contribution in early-stage than mature seep sediments, and nitrate/methane amendments increased net N2O production.
A methane-consuming animal–microbe assemblage developed within approximately one to two years at the monitored newborn seep, with aerobic and anaerobic methanotrophs and bioturbating fauna.
ANME-1 genomes contained variable hotspots associated with defense, transport, and methane-metabolism genes; heterologous hicAB tests supported toxin–antitoxin function.

Moderate sulfide shortage preserved symbiont abundance, whereas severe shortage coincided with reduced abundance and altered host lysosomal pathways; sulfur-metabolism responses indicated symbiotic flexibility.
The six sponge species hosted distinct bacterial assemblages, with SUP05 prominent in most samples.
